tap to select, press and hold on the map to place
Only one person per row and per column. It's up to you to cross out the squares that become impossible.
You can sit in an armchair or on a trunk, be in the bathtub, read a grimoire or drink a potion. Never on a bookcase, a cauldron, a mandrake, a desk, a candelabra, a mirror or the gramophone.
“Next to” means directly left, right, above or below, and in the same room.
The murderer is the only person alone in a room with the victim.
A crime has happened. Your goal: find where each person was, then unmask the murderer. Like sudoku, but with suspects.
Each card gives a clue about where the person was. The victim is in red.
The castle is split into squares and rooms. Only one person per row and per column.
You can sit in an armchair or on a trunk, be in the bathtub or read a grimoire. Hatched squares are off-limits (bookcase, cauldron, desk…).
Tap a suspect, then press and hold a square: the frame fills and the person is placed. Then remember to cross out their row and column yourself with the X tool.
A short tap just pencils the suspect's initial: handy for noting possible squares.
The X tool crosses out a square (drag to cross out several). The eraser clears. Undo goes back.
Scratchpad mode shows the map in black and white so you can scribble theories without touching your grid.
Hint gives you a real logical deduction, never a random answer.
The murderer is the only person alone in a room with the victim. Once everyone is placed, press Check. Happy sleuthing!
